topic: trump criticizes houthi behavior in yemen
headline_marked: Trump says [[Houthi rebels are misbehaving]] after Saudi airport attacks
headline: Trump says Houthi rebels are misbehaving after Saudi airport attacks
summary: US President Donald Trump expressed anger over repeated attacks on Saudi airports and fuel infrastructure by the Iran-backed Houthi group.
details: US President Donald Trump has expressed anger over the repeated attacks carried out by the Iran-backed Houthi armed group in Saudi Arabia.
When asked about his plans regarding the Houthis, Trump stated, "Actually, the Houthis are misbehaving very badly. This is not good at all."
The Houthis have launched continuous attacks on several Saudi airports, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
A Saturday attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport left at least 13 people dead and over 300 injured, with airport operations temporarily suspended.
A subsequent attack on Sunday left one person dead and 11 injured. Saudi authorities have announced that King Khalid International Airport will remain closed until next Saturday.
Beyond airports, the Houthis have also been targeting Saudi Arabia's fuel infrastructure, leading several airlines to cancel flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam.
Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways have temporarily suspended or cancelled flights to these cities due to the regional tension.
In Yemen, state media reported that Houthi shelling in the Taiz area of the southwestern region injured five people, including three children.
Separate shelling incidents in the Al-Dahra and Bir Basha districts of Taiziz also resulted in injuries to civilians, including a 30-year-old woman.

A Saturday attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport left at least 13 people dead and over 300 injured, with airport operations temporarily suspended.

A subsequent attack on Sunday left one person dead and 11 injured. Saudi authorities have announced that King Khalid International Airport will remain closed until next Saturday.

Beyond airports, the Houthis have also been targeting Saudi Arabia's fuel infrastructure, leading several airlines to cancel flights to Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam.

Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways have temporarily suspended or cancelled flights to these cities due to the regional tension.

In Yemen, state media reported that Houthi shelling in the Taiz area of the southwestern region injured five people, including three children.

Separate shelling incidents in the Al-Dahra and Bir Basha districts of Taiziz also resulted in injuries to civilians, including a 30-year-old woman.

topic: benapole port suspends trade for durga puja
headline_marked: Tk 160 crore revenue loss: [[Benapole port to suspend trade for 8 days]] during Durga Puja
headline: Tk 160 crore revenue loss: Benapole port to suspend trade for 8 days during Durga Puja
summary: Import-export activities will be paused from October 17 to 24 due to holidays in India and Bangladesh, potentially impacting raw material supplies.
details: Import-export activities through Benapole Land Port will be suspended for eight consecutive days from October 17 to 24 on the occasion of Durga Puja.
Ruhul Amin, acting director of Benapole Land Port, stated that the suspension is due to holidays at India's Petrapole port and in Bangladesh, with normal operations resuming on October 25.
Alhaj Mohsin Milon, president of the Benapole Port Importers and Exporters Association, noted that approximately 500 trucks cross the border daily, generating about Tk 20 crore in government revenue.
The eight-day suspension is expected to cause a revenue loss of around Tk 160 crore for the government.
Traders have expressed concerns over potential cargo congestion and traffic gridlock once operations resume, which could affect the supply of industrial raw materials and essential commodities.
While trade is paused, passenger movement through the Benapole-Petrapole international checkpost will continue as usual.
Customs clearance and internal port activities will remain operational on October 18 and 19 to clear previously imported goods and allow empty Indian trucks to return.
Immigration services will remain fully operational throughout the holiday period, with additional officials deployed to handle increased passenger traffic.
caption:
A potential Tk 160 crore revenue loss as Benapole Land Port pauses trade for 8 days.

Import-export activities through Benapole Land Port will be suspended for eight consecutive days from October 17 to 24 on the occasion of Durga Puja.

Ruhul Amin, acting director of Benapole Land Port, stated that the suspension is due to holidays at India's Petrapole port and in Bangladesh, with normal operations resuming on October 25.

Alhaj Mohsin Milon, president of the Benapole Port Importers and Exporters Association, noted that approximately 500 trucks cross the border daily, generating about Tk 20 crore in government revenue.

The eight-day suspension is expected to cause a revenue loss of around Tk 160 crore for the government.

Traders have expressed concerns over potential cargo congestion and traffic gridlock once operations resume, which could affect the supply of industrial raw materials and essential commodities.

While trade is paused, passenger movement through the Benapole-Petrapole international checkpost will continue as usual.

Customs clearance and internal port activities will remain operational on October 18 and 19 to clear previously imported goods and allow empty Indian trucks to return.

Immigration services will remain fully operational throughout the holiday period, with additional officials deployed to handle increased passenger traffic.
